Agenda Item#4
  Meeting Date: 2-22-2022

  MINUTES
  OF THE JANUARY 13, 2022 REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council was held via Zoom
videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to AB
361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s recommended measures to
promote social distancing. Members of the public were provided with the following
information to provide public input:

BYCOMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86156178569
Zoom Meeting ID: 861 5617 8569
BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code: 861 5617 8569#

CALL TO ORDER The meeting was called to order at 6:31 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE The pledge of Allegiance was suspended.

ROLL CALL

Present: Committee members Rossick, Nye, Rhodes, McCabe

Absent: Vice Chair Cooper

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Committee Member Rhodes, and seconded by Committee Member
Rossick to continue Item 2 to a later date at the request of the applicant. The motion carried
by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Rhodes, Nye, Rossick, McCabe
ABSENT: Cooper

 Parklands Committee Minutes
 January 13, 2022
 COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Mayor Victoria Lozzi addressed the committee to thank all members for the work they did in
2021 and for all the work they will do in 2022. She acknowledged the Committee’s dedicated
service to the community, the Committee’s responsiveness to the issues and concerns of
the residents. She stated the Parklands Committee was at the center of the most sensitive
issue of the City. She mentioned the parklands workshop last September, the City’s priority
to perform a tree inventory, and to develop a tree management plan that addresses the
issues surrounding trees holistically for the entire City. She discussed the encroachments
that the Committee had previously worked on and the policies regarding encroachments in
the Parklands. That project should be coming up to speed as soon as the new Code
Enforcement Officer settles in. She thanked the Committee again for their hard work and
wished them a happy New Year.

Mary Sheh addressed the Committee.

Committee Member Rhodes thanked the Mayor for her service and the two priorities she
mentioned were needed. Ms. Rhodes expressed the Committee’s appreciation that Council
is working on these issues.

CITIZEN APPLICATIONS

1.  PC-559-22; Application to remove one Canary Island pine and one Mexican Fan palm
located in the parkway adjacent to 612 Yarmouth Road

Applicant: Jay Adams, 612 Yarmouth Road, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Urban Forester Moritz shared a PowerPoint of the trees, indicating the application was for
the removal of a Canary Island pine and a Mexican Fan palm. He noted the designated
street tree for this road is a Holly Oak (Quercus ilex). The location of the trees are adjacent to
612 Yarmouth Road, the same location as the applicant. He advised the reason for the
application was safety, advising the trees were in good health. The City received numerous
letters in support of the removal of the trees.

The Urban Forester advised the committee members that in considering non-view related
applications, the Parklands Committee must seek to strike reasonable balance between
preservation and enhancement of mature trees and the protection of privacy and
preservation and enhancement of public safety of each property owner as outlined in
Resolution No. R18-13, the Tree Management Policy; and shall respect the neighborhood
character and should not make a recommendation that would result in significantly altering
the unique feeling of a particular neighborhood.

The neighborhood character of Yarmouth Road is Holly Oaks which was designated as the
street tree in 2001 and was well represented on the block. The Canary Island pine and
Mexican Fan palm have never been the designated street trees. The Canary Island pine
and Mexican Fan palm were randomly planted in the neighborhood in very small numbers

 Parklands Committee Minutes
 January 13, 2022
 and appear to be out of place with the Oak trees and the neighborhood character.

The Urban Forester advised the Mexican Fan palms were considered an invasive tree in
southern California and not recommended for planting due to high potential for disease to
start growing in the Parklands. He noted that the property has a multitude of trees and
privacy will not be an issue if the trees were removed. The Parklands Committee should
also consider to the extent reasonably practicable the preservation and enhancement of
public safety. He stated the reason for the application is safety. The pine tree is the main
culprit in that there seems to be some disruption in the pavers which are being displaced by
the pine roots and will continue to lift as the roots increase in diameter. There is also concern
about the squirrels climbing the tree and chewing the green pinecones causing them to fall
creating a propensity for damage to cars.

Urban Forester Moritz presented a photograph of the property depicting two Holly Oaks, one
of which is overshadowed by the pine tree which has suppressed the Holly Oaks’ growth.
Staff recommended the Committee recommend approval to the City Council for the removal
of one Canary Island pine and one Mexican Fan palm according to the standards and
conditions for tree removal approvals, require a $1000 payment be made to the Tree Bank,
require a tree permit, and removal of both stumps.

Committee member Nye expressed concern about the driveway not being the reason to
remove the trees explaining that having pavers could be removed to cut tree roots to prevent
uplifting the driveway and confirmed that was not the reason for removal of the tree.

Committee member Rossick advised she walks that area and confirmed the droppings
coming from the pine trees.

Mr. Moritz confirmed that the Pine tree could grow another ten feet in height and the roots
and diameter could grow three times the height of the tree.

ACTION: Moved by Committee Member Rossick, and seconded by Committee Member
Nye, to open the public hearing. Committee Member Rhodes recused herself due to a
conflict and left the meeting. The motion carried by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Rossick, Nye, McCabe
ABSENT: Cooper
ABSTAIN BY RECUSAL: Rhodes

The Applicant, Jay and Regan Adams addressed the Committee.

The following individuals, as identified by the names on their Zoom screens, addressed the
Committee:
Betty
Mary Sheh
Monique Thorrington
Shikha
Maureen McGowan

 Parklands Committee Minutes
 January 13, 2022
 Suk Kunoth

The Committee members addressed the issues, asked questions, and expressed their
opinions.

Committee Member Nye and Rossick both clarified that the reason they were voting in favor
of the removal was because of the safety concerns and the fact that the street tree behind it
will get an opportunity to grow once the pine is removed. Chair McCabe reiterated his
colleagues’ concerns stating that the Committee does value the trees and that it was not an
easy decision for the Committee; however, in considering this application, the safety issue
is what concerns him.

ACTION: Moved by Committee Member Nye, and seconded by Committee Member
Rossick, to close the public hearing. The motion carried by the members present.

ACTION: Committee Member Nye moved, and seconded by Committee Member Rossick,
to remove the Canary Island pine and on Mexican Fan palm from 612 Yarmouth Road. The
motion carried by the following roll call vote:
AYES: Rossick, Nye, McCabe
ABSENT: Cooper
ABSTAIN BY RECUSAL: Rhodes

Committee Member Rhodes re-entered the meeting.

2.  PC-561-22; Application to remove four Aleppo pines, one Canary Island pine and
three Olives, all located in the parkways adjacent to 1252, 1256, 1260, 1300, 1305, 1309,
and 1313 Via Romero

  Applicant: John Weick, 1309 Via Romero, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Item 2 was continued to a future date (no date set).

ITEMS OF INFORMATION FROM THE COMMITTEE/STAFF

Urban Forester Moritz announced that on Monday, the City will start the fire safety weed
abatement project to address the parklands.

Committee Member Rossick asked about the nine pines that were removed from 1248 or
1249 Via Romero.

Urban Forester Moritz responded that the tree that is still on 1248 Via Romero is a Stone
pine and it was on private property. The owner did not have permission from the Homes
Association and it was reported to the HOA and the work was stopped because of the
worksite was unsafe due to lack of traffic control. The owners at 1249 Via Romero had
approval to remove six Canary Island pines and somehow seven were removed, which was
also reported to the Homes Association.

 Parklands Committee Minutes
 January 13, 2022
 In response to a question posed by Committee Member Rossick, Mr. Moritz explained the
difference between a city tree and a private tree resulting in a discussion as to when the City
has authority over a tree and when the Homeowners Association has authority.

Chair McCabe thanked the Mayor for her warm welcome acknowledging the appreciation
the Committee receives from the Council. He also confirmed on behalf of all the committee
members that they intend to continue to work hard.

He also shared that the Agenda was supposed to have a discussion regarding the sub-
committee on the Agenda this evening but there was an apparent lack of communication.
He has been told it will absolutely be on the March agenda so they can break out and do
some work on the items discussed at the September joint meeting with the City Council.

Committee Member Rhodes encouraged the neighbors in the area of Item 2 to try to come
to a compromise.

There being no further business to come before the committee, the meeting was adjourned
at 7:36 pm.

RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED

_______________________________
Carol Cowley

 January 13, 2022
